edges.relation: Sync point discovery provides the candidate positions that speculative block boundary detection validates
Both use speculative parallelism: block detection speculates on position, FSM speculation speculates on state
Bitstream swizzling is the format-level prerequisite for GPU warp-parallel decoding to work efficiently
Both reorganize data layout for parallelism; swizzling operates at bit level, interleaving at stream level
ANS naturally supports stream interleaving (Giesen 2014), making it the ideal entropy coder for multi-stream decode
Multi-stream decode multiplies table access pressure, making cache-optimized table layout critical
FPGA dual-path decode is a hardware instantiation of the FSM speculative parallelism concept
GPU warps can execute multiple speculative FSM paths simultaneously using thread-level parallelism
GPU shared memory acts as an explicit managed cache; prefetch strategies apply to both CPU and GPU LZ77 copy
Neural model can predict ANS state distributions for faster table construction, or pre-warm tANS decode tables
Both optimize the LZ77 copy inner loop: prefetch hides latency, branchless removes control-flow overhead
Prefetch effectiveness depends on data layout; restructured memory improves prefetch hit rates
GPU architectures naturally execute branchless (predicated) code; LZ77 unification maps directly to SIMT execution
FPGA speculative paths can implement hardware-accelerated block boundary detection with clock-cycle granularity
Predicted code distributions enable pre-optimized table layouts before actual decoding begins
Discovered sync points define cache-coherent decompression segments that can be prefetched independently
Compact table layout reduces working set size, enabling more speculative FSM paths to fit in cache simultaneously
